help.intro: A short text of about 130 words about the strangest market in Germany: the Hamburg fish market, which opens every Sunday at five in the morning, has done so since 1703, and where the sellers shout their prices and throw bananas and eels into bags. The facts are real and were checked. You need what you have just learnt: plural forms of food words (Fische, Bananen, Äpfel, Blumen), the articles in the nominative, numbers and prices (zehn Euro, fünf Uhr), and the question words Wann? (when), Was? (what), Wer? (who). Read for the gist first, then answer each question from one sentence of the text.
help.tips[0].title: Plurals at the market
help.tips[0].text: der Fisch → die Fische, der Apfel → die Äpfel, die Banane → die Bananen, die Blume → die Blumen, der Aal → die Aale, die Tüte → die Tüten, der Euro → stays Euro after a number (zehn Euro), die Uhr → fünf Uhr (time, no plural). Many feminine nouns take -n or -en; many masculine nouns take -e, sometimes with umlaut (Äpfel).
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Ten bananas, five apples and three fish in one bag.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The bag costs only ten euros!
help.tips[0].check.q: What is the plural of der Apfel?
help.tips[0].check.why: Apfel takes an umlaut and no ending: Äpfel.
help.tips[1].text: Wann? asks for a time or a day: am Sonntag, um fünf Uhr, seit 1703. Um fünf Uhr = at five o'clock; von fünf bis halb zehn = from five to half past nine (halb zehn is 9:30, half before ten!). Seit = since: seit 1703, seit dreihundert Jahren.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The market starts at five o'clock and ends at half past nine.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The fish market has existed since 1703.
help.tips[1].check.why: halb zehn = half (on the way) to ten = 9:30. Careful: not half past ten.
help.remember[0]: Plurals: Fische, Äpfel, Bananen, Blumen, Tüten; zehn Euro stays Euro.
help.remember[1]: um fünf Uhr = at five; halb zehn = 9:30; seit 1703 = since 1703.
help.exam: Short texts about markets, shopping and times with multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: Sunday, five in the morning, and thousands of people buy fish, bananas and flowers while the sellers shout. Read about Hamburg's wildest market.
passageTranslation:
It is Sunday, five o'clock in the morning. In Hamburg almost everyone is asleep. But at the harbour it is loud. Here is the fish market.

The fish market has existed since 1703. That is over three hundred years! It is open every Sunday, from five o'clock to half past nine. In winter it starts at seven o'clock.

What is there here? Fish, of course: eels, salmon and prawns. But also fruit and vegetables, flowers, cheese, bread and clothes. The sellers shout loudly: 'Ten bananas, two pineapples and five kiwis, all together only ten euros!' They throw the bananas into a bag. The people laugh and buy.

The most famous seller is called Aale-Dieter. He has sold eels at the fish market for over fifty years. He shouts very loudly and makes many jokes.

Many people come straight from the party. They dance a little more in the fish auction hall, drink coffee and eat a fish roll. Then they go home and sleep.
questions[0].explanation: "Er ist jeden Sonntag offen, von fünf Uhr bis halb zehn."
questions[0].questionTranslation: When is the fish market open?
questions[0].optionsTranslation[1]: every Sunday from five o'clock to half past nine
questions[0].optionsTranslation[2]: every Saturday evening from five to half past nine
questions[1].explanation: "Den Fischmarkt gibt es seit 1703. Das ist über dreihundert Jahre!"
questions[1].questionTranslation: Since when has the fish market existed?
questions[2].explanation: "Im Winter beginnt er um sieben Uhr."
questions[2].questionTranslation: At what time does the market start in winter?
questions[3].explanation: The text lists fish, fruit and vegetables, flowers, cheese, bread and clothes. No cars.
questions[3].questionTranslation: What is there NOT at the fish market?
questions[4].questionTranslation: What does the bag with ten bananas, two pineapples and five kiwis cost?
questions[5].explanation: "Der berühmteste Verkäufer heißt Aale-Dieter. Er verkauft seit über fünfzig Jahren Aale …"
questions[6].explanation: "Er verkauft … Aale … Er ruft sehr laut und macht viele Witze."
questions[6].optionsTranslation[0]: He sells flowers and bread and is very quiet and friendly.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[1]: He sells eels, shouts loudly and makes jokes.
questions[7].explanation: "Dann gehen sie nach Hause und schlafen."
questions[7].questionTranslation: What do the people from the party do at the end?
help.tips[1].title: Wann? Um wie viel Uhr?
